title: PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE REPORT and PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE REPORT relative to illegal dumping enforcement, Fiscal Year 2026-27 funding, and related matters.…
text:
[Council File 26-1351]
[Items for which Public Hearings Have Been Held]
PUBLIC WORKS COMMITTEE REPORT and PUBLIC SAFETY COMMITTEE REPORT relative to illegal dumping enforcement, Fiscal Year 2026-27 funding, and related matters. A. Public Works Committee Report Recommendations for Council action, as initiated by Motion (Padilla, Harris-Dawson - Price):
1. INSTRUCT the Bureau of Street Services (BSS), in coordination with the Bureau of Sanitation (BOS), Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), City Attorney, and other relevant City departments, to report to the City Council within 30 days on illegal dumping enforcement activities and the status of funding allocated in the Fiscal Year 2026-27 budget. This report should include recommendations on needed resources and funding for strengthening the City's response to illegal dumping toward a comprehensive strategy of abatement, prevention, and enforcement.
2. INSTRUCT the BSS to report on the feasibility of utilizing existing City contracts, technology, equipment, and other resources currently available to City departments, including BOS and LAPD, for the limited purpose of identifying, documenting, investigating, and prosecuting illegal dumping activity.
3. INSTRUCT the BSS, in coordination with each Council District office, to develop a citywide inventory of chronic illegal dumping hotspots, with each Council District identifying priority locations within its jurisdiction, and report on a system for regularly updating the inventory based on both objective City data and community and Council District input.
4. REQUEST the City Attorney, with assistance from the Chief Legislative Analyst (CLA), LAPD, and BOS, to report with options to update penalties for illegal dumping, as well as increasing rewards for successful prosecutions, to align with other municipalities in California. B. Public Safety Committee Report dated October 6, 2026 Recommendations for Council action, pursuant to Motion (Harris-Dawson, Padilla - Price):
1. INSTRUCT the Bureau of Street Services (BSS), in coordination with Los Angeles Sanitation and Environment (LASAN), Los Angeles Police Department (LAPD), City Attorney, and other relevant City departments, to report within 30 days on illegal dumping enforcement activities, the status of funding allocated in the Fiscal Year 2026-27 Budget, and recommendations for additional resources and funding to strengthen abatement, prevention, and enforcement.
2. INSTRUCT BSS to report on the feasibility of utilizing existing City contracts, technology, equipment, and other departmental resources, including those of LASAN and LAPD, to identify, document, investigate, and prosecute illegal dumping activity.
3. INSTRUCT BSS, in coordination with each Council District office, to develop a citywide inventory of chronic illegal dumping hotspots and report on a system for regularly updating the inventory using City data and community and Council District input.
4. INSTRUCT BSS, in coordination with LAPD and LASAN, to report within 30 days with options to update illegal dumping penalties and increase rewards for successful prosecutions, consistent with practices in other California municipalities.
Fiscal Impact Statement:
Neither the City Administrative Officer nor the CLA has completed a financial analysis of this report.
Community Impact Statement:
None submitted
(Energy and Environment Committee has waived consideration of this matter)
summary: Motion on funding illegal dumping enforcement for fiscal year 2026-27. It is in committee, and the Public Safety Committee approved it on October 6, 2026.
